headline: Beforepay CEO flags FY27 as a strong outlook year as full-year repricing and volume tailwinds flow through, with personal loans surging 728% and profitability up 57%.
reasoning: Beforepay delivered its most profitable year on record with cash NPAT up 57% to $15.7 million and revenue up 26% to over $50 million, driven by higher pay-advance volumes and the introduction of interest on pay advances. CEO Jamie Twiss highlighted that FY26 numbers only captured partial-year effects of repricing and volume growth, meaning FY27 will see the full run-rate benefit. Approximately $12.5 million of annualised interest income from the new pay-advance pricing is expected to flow almost entirely to the bottom line, with less than $2 million recognised in FY26. Personal loans surged 728% to $16.9 million and Twiss sees the multi-billion-dollar consumer unsecured lending market as a large disruption opportunity given Beforepay's 2 million registered users and credit risk sophistication. The company has also nearly doubled its debt funding capacity, providing headroom for aggressive growth, and is rolling out a new generation of credit risk models.
quote: So I think the outlook for FY 27 is very strong, because some of the pricing and other initiatives we put through are really going to take effect and have a noticeable impact next year. So there are a couple of different things driving it. One is simply a run rate effect. So the FY 26 numbers have partial years of repricing, partial years of the increases in volumes. But those are going to continue through FY 27 at the current rate. And that by itself gives us a tremendous tailwind. We also were best known for our sophistication around credit risk management. And we are releasing and updating a new generation of risk models that we think will give us a even sharper view of individuals and what the right loan offer for them is at any point in time.
episode_title: Beforepay’s digital lending flywheel starts spinning

headline: Observes pockets of financial stress in Australian economy, particularly where wages are not keeping pace with cost of living
reasoning: As one of the largest aggregators of bank transaction data in Australia, Beforepay has granular visibility into household financial stress. Management notes pockets of stress in specific professions where wages are not keeping up and in higher cost-of-living areas. Despite this, the company's own credit risk models have kept repayment rates at approximately 99%, suggesting that while broader macro stress is visible, Beforepay's underwriting remains insulated through careful model adjustments.
quote: We do see there are certainly pockets of stress more broadly in the Australian economy. We're one of the largest aggregators of bank transaction data in the country. And so we can see where individual, for example, professions where the wages may not be keeping up or in higher cost areas, we can see that stress emerging and we watch that carefully.
episode_title: Beforepay’s digital lending flywheel starts spinning

headline: Beforepay CEO highlights strong user growth, disciplined credit risk management and AI-driven efficiency as key investment pillars
reasoning: Beforepay has 2 million registered users and is writing approximately 40,000 loans per week with only 50 staff, making it one of the most efficient lenders in the world. The company uses AI extensively in its credit risk models, analysing billions of data points to assess affordability and repayment intent. Credit performance is strong, with roughly 99% of borrowers repaying on time, supported by nimble risk-setting adjustments when macro conditions tighten. Management is focused on continuing steady revenue and profit growth as the key metric by which investors should judge the business. Beforepay is also one of the largest aggregators of bank transaction data in Australia, giving it early visibility into pockets of economic stress. The CEO indicated the company is open to M&A or corporate activity on a shareholder-value basis but is not actively seeking a transaction.
quote: So we currently are writing about 40,000 loans every week and the whole company is 50 people. So we are one of the most efficient lenders in the world. And I would be surprised if anyone in Australia could meet that. So we we will see if that number comes down even further. But already the ability to write 2 million loans in one year with such a small team, I think is a pretty good testament to efficiency. We use it quite a bit. So we have some very sophisticated risk models that use quite a bit of AI in that creation phase, in order to look at literally billions of data points and work out in a way that is much sharper than is common practice. What can this customer afford? What can we see about them behaviorally? What's their personality and their intent to repay? So I don't think we would exist in our current form without AI. It's a bedrock of what we do.
episode_title: Beforepay’s digital lending flywheel starts spinning
